answer: An agent economy can bind each account to a rotating, randomly sampled network of established agents that must vouch for its history and escrow stake before it may trade. New identities begin with no trust, while conflicting vouches trigger audits and slash the sponsors’ deposits. A Sybil operator therefore must acquire many independent endorsements and lock capital across the meadow, atlas, and mesa markets; fabricating names alone produces no buying power and makes collusion expensive to sustain.
